messages:
incident-bot: Pager: Private VPC cluster (cust-acme) GPU queue growth above 95% for 15m, autoscaler failing: scale_attempts=12, failures=12. Impact: inference requests throttled. Severity: P1.

sam (oncall): Got it. I'm taking pager. initial triage: confirmed elevated queue on nodepool 'nv-gpu-pool-1' in us-west-2. Autoscaler logs show repeated 'Node provisioning timed out' and 'ImagePullBackOff' for new nodes.

maria (infra): seeing the same. cloud provider reports 'insufficient instance capacity' for g4dn-like shapes in that AZ. Also, the AMI bake step is failing at 35% with timeout (we've had a couple of bad bakes this week).

jordan (eng-sre): @sam can you paste the autoscaler error lines? I want to see if it's the cluster autoscaler or our custom provisioner.

sam (oncall): pasted below from logs:

```
2026-03-15T10:04:12Z scale-manager: scaleAttempt start pool=nv-gpu-pool-1 target=6
2026-03-15T10:05:45Z provisioner: createInstance id=req-2314 status=failed reason=ImagePullBackOff
2026-03-15T10:06:50Z scale-manager: scaleAttempt failed pool=nv-gpu-pool-1 reason=provision_timeout
```

ben (runtime): Runtime reports growing pending queues for customer models using dedicated nodes. Latency SLOs failing for multiple customers. We have auto-fallback to cpu-variant but that's off for private clusters.

eve (cs): Customer on the line (cust-acme) reports degraded inference. They're seeing requeued requests and timeouts. They're escalating.

sam (oncall): Immediate mitigations I'm trying:
- bumping scale limit on pool from 10 -> 20 (if cloud capacity available)
- enabling fallback route to smaller gpu type in config
- temporarily allow cpu fallback for non-sensitive requests

maria (infra): Attempted to increase pool limit but cloud API returned 'instance-quotas-exceeded' for us-west-2. Request to quota team is in flight (ticket #Q-4821).

jordan (eng-sre): If provisioning is failing due to AMI bake, we can skip bake and use standby AMI version that is known-good. Ben, do runtime images need the latest kernel patch or can we use last stable AMI?

ben (runtime): We can run with the last stable AMI (ami-0stable123) for emergency. It lacks a new telemetry agent but inference runtime will run fine. I'd prefer this to blocking customer workloads.

sam (oncall): maria, can you trigger a manual node group creation with ami-0stable123 into that pool? I can hold the front door to avoid further autoscaler churn.

maria (infra): Manual creation started: `gcloud compute instances create --image=ami-0stable123 --count=4 --zone=us-west2-a ...` I'll keep you updated. If cloud capacity refuses, alternative AZ possible.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: manual-add-nodes -> nv-gpu-pool-1 (4 nodes). ETA ~ 7m.

jordan (eng-sre): Also recommend turning on short-lived admission throttle at the front (drop non-essential reroutes) to keep tail latency for critical customers.

sam (oncall): Doing that now: enabling admission policy 'critical-only' for cust-acme and cust-beta. Will post when live.

ben (runtime): Observability note: enabling admission reduces incoming token rate by ~40% for background workloads. Good short-term.

maria (infra): Cloud finally accepted 2 nodes in alternate AZ; 2 remained pending due to capacity. New nodes joined cluster at 2026-03-15T10:12Z (2 nodes).

sam (oncall): queue length stabilizing, pending jobs draining onto new nodes. Latency improving for cust-acme. Still watching for retries and backpressure.

eve (cs): Confirmed with customer: service responsiveness improving. They've paused escalation but want incident timeline and RCA.

jordan (eng-sre): Next steps:
- finish AMI bake investigation (probable regression in init script)
- add fallback AMI in autoscaler config
- document runbook for manual AMI switchover
- quota request follow-up with cloud team

sam (oncall): Handing off to eng-sre postmortem. I'll keep the channel open for any re-escalations. Thanks all :tada:

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to 'resolved' by sam at 2026-03-15T10:25:45Z. Postmortem assigned to eng-sre; severity downgraded to P2 for RCA tracking.
